jobs.title: Data Science and Analytics Leader
jobs.description:
At Delta Faucet
, we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence.

Your Role at Delta Faucet:

Are you passionate about using data science to propel decisions? If you are interested in crafting the smart connected home of the future - this is an opportunity to join the market-leading Delta Faucet Company team as we use analytics to turbocharge product development and business decisions!

Reporting to the Sr. Director of Insights and Analytics, this role will accompany a team of research and domain specialists excited to deploy advanced analytics throughout the business. You will lead practitioners to develop advanced models, influence the IoT architecture, and grow our data and literacy.

Responsibilities:

We are seeking a player/coach to lead our advanced analytics capability, specifically you will:

Reinforce data driven behaviors across the enterprise, moving analytic insight to actions.
Explore, build, and pilot analytic solutions to enhance business decisions.
Craft an experimental framework, including use of artificial intelligence agents to accelerate product development.
Deliver market insights to socialize product mix, competitor performance, and pricing detail.
Generate and synthesize economic, market, and consumer insights· Develop a hardworking team of analytics specialists and data scientists.
Brainstorm and implement analytics initiatives that make a difference for the enterprise.
Lead academic data science partnerships.
Coordinate application of statistical frameworks to inform the organizations strategy

The role will also join a cross-functional leadership team influencing the architecture and development of data platforms to enable data science

Education & Experience:

A successful candidate will be a lifelong learner who has:

3+ years architecting analytic solutions for sales, marketing, or manufacturing
3+ years crafting data visualizations using Power BI, Python, R-Shiny, or Tableau
3+ years of applied data science experience using R or Python
2+ years cross functional initiative experience
2+ years of talent development or teambuilding managerial experience
Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics or other related degree

Why Join Us?

At Delta Faucet Company, our people are our greatest assets. We value different perspectives and fostering an inclusive environment. You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our brand, working alongside passionate professionals committed to excellence and innovation. Join us to lead progressive growth and make a significant impact within a leading organization.

Here are some of the benefits we offer for your personal and professional growth:

Culture: Recognized and award-winning reputation for equality, diversity and inclusion, flexibility, work-life balance, and more.
Wellbeing: Comprehensive benefit plans; retirement, savings, tuition reimbursement, and employee incentive programs; resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Learning & Development: LinkedIn Learning access; internal opportunities to work on projects cross-company.
Social Impact: Four employee-led and self-directed Business Resource Groups; Paid volunteer day annually; Employees share their time, skills and talent with charities and nonprofit organizations across the U.S. and around the globe.

Company: Delta Faucet Company

Full time

jobs.title: Sr. Back-End CAD Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Layout Automation & Physical Verification

About The Role

Micron is seeking a Senior CAD Automation Engineer to develop custom-layout automation and physical-verification methodologies for next-generation DRAM, HBM, NAND, and emerging memory technologies.

This role owns automation and enablement spanning layout creation, PCells, layout generators, DRC/LVS/ERC, parasitic extraction, and signoff. You will partner with custom-layout, circuit-design, process, PDK, and verification teams to deliver correct-by-construction methodologies and scalable verification flows. You will also help drive the adoption of AI-enabled engineering workflows
to improve efficiency, debugging, and build quality.

What You'll Do

Build custom-layout automation, PCells, layout generators, and layout methodologies guided by build rules.
Build and maintain Cadence Virtuoso and SKILL-based efficiency solutions.
Develop, qualify, and deploy DRC, LVS, ERC, PERC, antenna, density, and extraction flows.
Integrate layout databases with Calibre, Pegasus, PVS, Quantus, StarRC, or related signoff platforms.
Automate verification setup, distributed execution, results processing, reporting, and debug.
Support rule-deck qualification, PDK releases, process-rule interpretation, and foundry or process-team enablement.
Develop correct-by-construction checks that prevent common layout and verification errors.
Build automation through Python, SKILL, Tcl, C++, OpenAccess, or design-database APIs.
Track verification efficiency, error escape rate, runtime, capacity, and flow stability.
Apply AI/ML and LLM-assisted techniques to error classification, log analysis, layout debugging, and support workflows.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
5+ years of experience in CAD, EDA, semiconductor design, or design automation.
Require proven experience in at least two of the following:
Virtuoso/SKILL layout automation
DRC/LVS physical-verification methodology
PCell or layout-generator development
PDK or rule-deck enablement
Parasitic extraction or layout signoff

Strong programming skills in Python.
Linux/Unix and shell scripting experience.
CMOS and VLSI fundamentals.

**This is a semiconductor design-automation position. It is not a mechanical CAD, PCB layout, drafting, AutoCAD, or general software back-end engineering role.**

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Virtuoso Layout Suite, PCells, layout generators, and layout methods guided by specific build rules.
Experience developing or supporting Siemens Calibre verification flows including DRC, LVS, nmDRC, nmLVS, RVE, and SVRF rule decks.
Knowledge of ERC, PERC, antenna checks, density verification, and layout-dependent effects (LDE).
Experience with OpenAccess, design database APIs, or GUI development frameworks such as Python Qt.
Experience with parasitic extraction, signoff methodologies, and process rule development.
Experience applying AI/ML, LLMs, or agentic AI technologies to engineering workflows.
Experience with source control, automated testing, and release management.

jobs.description:
Overview

Handshake is looking for experienced mechanical, manufacturing, and quality engineers, as well as CNC programmers, to support AI research through flexible, part-time contract work. This is not a traditional engineering role—you'll draw on your hands-on experience in mechanical design, structural and thermal analysis, injection molding and tooling, manufacturing processes, or engineering change and quality control to evaluate AI-generated content and provide feedback that helps AI reason like a practicing engineer. This is an ongoing, project-based opportunity that you can take on alongside your current role or studies.

What You'll Do

Create expert-level mechanical engineering problems and scenarios grounded in real design, analysis, tooling, manufacturing, and quality work that gets built, tested, or approved
Review AI-generated responses for technical accuracy, practical feasibility, manufacturability, and alignment with industry standards and engineering practice
Evaluate models, drawings, tolerances, calculations, and simulation results for correctness, defensibility, and whether a reviewer could work from them
Provide clear, structured written feedback to help improve AI model performance
Complete tasks at your own pace, with no set schedule or minimum-hour requirement

Qualifications

Industry experience — working mechanical engineer or current undergraduate/graduate student who has personally produced a part, assembly, or analysis that someone else manufactured, tested, or approved from
Degree — BS, MS, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related engineering field
A degree is not required if you are a CNC programmer.
If you are in the process of completing your bachelor's degree, internship experience is required.

Domain expertise — demonstrated depth in one or more of the following areas:
Mechanical design
Structural analysis (FEA)
Thermal and fluids
Injection molding and tooling
Manufacturing processes
Sustaining, quality, and configuration engineering

Additional Qualifications

These are not required but will strengthen your application:

Proficiency with tools such as SolidWorks, Creo, NX, CATIA, Inventor, Fusion 360, ANSYS, Abaqus, Nastran, Fluent, STAR-CCM+, OpenFOAM, MATLAB, or comparable modeling, simulation, and CAM environments
Experience producing manufacturing-ready drawings or models — for machining, sheet metal, casting, injection molding, or additive processes
Experience at a manufacturer, product design firm, aerospace/defense contractor, automotive supplier

Based in the United States

Our Applied Science and ML Engineering teams build AI capabilities across Large Language Models (LLMs), image and video generation, and multimodal understanding. We partner with talented scientists, engineers, product managers, and business leaders to improve experiences for customers, associates, advertisers, and creators, while delivering measurable business outcomes. We are committed to exceeding industry standards through cutting-edge research, strong engineering execution, and responsible AI practices. Role Summary The Senior Manager, Data Science will lead an Applied Science and ML Engineering team within Retail AI Foundations. This leader will set the scientific and technical direction for production AI systems, working backward from customer needs and business priorities to define the problems, success measures, and investments that matter most. What You’ll Do

Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing team of Applied Scientists and ML Engineers.
Define the technical roadmap and science investment strategy for LLMs, image and video generation, multimodal understanding, agentic simulation, and multi-agent systems.
Translate priority business opportunities and customer-experience needs into AI product strategy, technical priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Lead the end-to-end development of ML and GenAI capabilities, including data strategy, experimentation, model development, evaluation, deployment, and iteration.
Partner across product, engineering, data, and business teams to deliver solutions for AI Shopping, Social Commerce, Walmart Connect, creator experiences, marketing, and rich-media content.
Establish standards for model quality, safety, reliability, latency, scalability, and responsible AI.
Guide architecture and model decisions spanning proprietary and open-weight models, post-training, fine-tuning, retrieval, and agentic workflows.
Communicate strategy, technical tradeoffs, model performance, and business impact to senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

What You’ll Bring

Strong expertise in machine learning, deep learning, NLP, information retrieval, analytics, and model evaluation.
Experience delivering complex ML systems, particularly across Generative AI, computer vision, multimodal AI, or deep learning.
Ability to turn customer and business needs into clear technical requirements, model designs, and scalable production solutions.
Strong cross-functional communication skills, including the ability to align product, engineering, technical teams, and leadership.
Experience with distributed training and inference frameworks, large-scale model serving, and massively parallel GPU systems.

2+ years of people-management experience leading Applied Scientists, Data Scientists, or ML Engineers, and 7+ years of experience building machine learning models or algorithms for business applications.
Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, Engineering, Robotics, Operations Research, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field; or equivalent practical experience.
Experience with LLM post-training and alignment, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, RLHF, DPO, or related techniques.
Experience with image or video generation models, multimodal understanding models, or production computer-vision systems.

About Sanguine Biosciences, Inc.

Sanguine Biosciences is accelerating personalized medicine research by empowering patients with their healthcare data and making it as easy as possible for them to participate in the medical research process. We partner with patients and pharmaceutical companies to accelerate precision medicine R&D by securely and efficiently collecting and providing patient samples and relevant health data. We are helping thousands of researchers at 20 of the top 40 global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies increase the speed and quality at which they are conducting their research. It is an exciting time; our biotech company is growing quickly and needs the best team members to join us.

The Laboratory Technician I is an entry-level role responsible for the processing of human whole blood and other human biospecimens used for research. Sample processing includes plasma, serum, PBMC, T, B, and NK cell isolations, cell counting, aliquot preparation, sample thawing, and sample storage procedures.

Technicians work primarily in the processing team and rotate into the fulfillment team (kitting, shipping, and sample retrieval) on a scheduled basis. The role works under direct guidance from team leads and senior technicians, builds toward independent sign-off on laboratory procedures, and may progress to Laboratory Technician II.

Primary Responsibilities

Sample Processing & Accessioning
Accurately document and accession biospecimen collection information following company SOPs.
Process whole blood into plasma, serum, and PBMC, including density gradient separation and cryopreservation of PBMCs, following SOPs and with direct guidance until each procedure is signed off.
Process other human biological samples as trained, including urine, stool, saliva, leukopaks, synovial fluid, and skin punch biopsies.
Assist with isolation of immune cell subsets such as T, B, and NK cells from whole blood.
Conduct cell counting, aliquot preparation, and sample thawing.
Assist with routine sample QC, including post-thaw viability, under guidance.
Perform basic laboratory procedures such as cell-based assay work, and assist with flow cytometry and research-grade testing.
Document all work completely, accurately, and at the time it is performed, including sample processing, specimen storage, distribution and transfers, and LIMS entries, in accordance with company standards.
Fulfillment, Rotation & Cross-Training
Prepare and pack biological samples for shipment under guidance, following SOPs and IATA regulations.
Support kit builds and frozen shipment prep on a scheduled rotation with the fulfillment team.
Coordinate and schedule kit shipments with approved couriers in line with established shipping procedures and customer requirements.
Receive, unpack, verify, process incoming deliveries, and help with supply counts and stock levels under the direction of the Biorepository Logistics Lead.
Complete cross-training on a backup team and maintain a current competency record.
Equipment, Safety & Compliance
Support basic troubleshooting of processing and sample storage equipment and escalate issues to team leads.
Participate in the rotating on-call for freezer and system alarms after training.
Participate in a rotating schedule to cover occasional weekend needs, such as special cases and sample deliveries, as required.
Perform routine laboratory equipment maintenance, cleaning, waste disposal, and general laboratory housekeeping in accordance with established SOPs, manufacturer guidelines, and company quality and safety standards. Ensure equipment and workspaces are clean, organized, and maintained in proper working condition, with all activities appropriately documented.
Perform routine laboratory support functions alongside the Biorepository Associates, such as labeling and organizing tubes and racks, preparing workstations and consumables, putting samples away with LIMS location updates, completing freezer and refrigerator temperature checks and equipment logs.
Flag unclear steps, errors, or gaps in the SOPs used to the team lead so they can be corrected.
Follow the company quality management system (QMS), approved SOPs, work instructions, and Good Documentation Practices (GDP), and comply with applicable regulatory and biosafety requirements, to ensure accurate and reproducible work.
Follow safety and EHS procedures, and perform other job functions or special projects as assigned.

Associate’s degree with at least 1 year of experience in a life science laboratory environment, or [2]+ years as a Biorepository Associate (I or II)
Ability to communicate effectively in verbal and written form.
Intermediate computer skills.
Complete cross-training and be signed off on kit build within 6 months of hire, and on frozen shipment prep under guidance within 12 months.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a life science field
Experience with mammalian blood samples.
Experience working in a biobank or biorepository.

Working Conditions

Must be willing to adhere to infectious disease and immunization protocols.
Must be able to work in a BSL-2 laboratory environment with biohazards and various chemicals and wear appropriate PPE.
Must be able to wear appropriate PPE.
Availability to work full-time shifts Monday through Friday between 7 AM and 7 PM, with occasional weekend availability as needed.

About The Role

As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain biology software in genomics and structural biology (libraries, command-line tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks) for use by researchers and AI agents, inside Anthropic and externally
Own the path from research code to public release, including testing, validation against reference data and established tools, benchmarking, documentation, and packaging, and make the call on when something is ready to ship
Maintain what we release: triage issues, review outside contributions, and manage breaking changes
Represent the team in the biology community through conferences, workshops, tutorials, and direct work with researchers and maintainers, and turn what you learn about their needs into priorities for the team
Partner with the team's computational and experimental scientists to turn research code into well-tested, reusable software
Lead the technical direction of the projects you own through design review, code review, and mentoring, and, depending on your interests and the team's needs, lead a small team
Build with Claude and AI coding agents as your default way of working, hold agent-written code to the same standard as your own, and set the team's practices for reviewing and validating it

Minimum Qualifications

Have built, released, and maintained biology software that researchers outside your own group use, with evidence of adoption you can point to (for example public repositories, package downloads, citations, or use in other groups' pipelines)
Have deep working expertise in genomics or structural biology, including the data types, file formats, standard tools, and common failure modes of at least one of these fields
Are proficient in Python and comfortable working with large datasets in Linux and cloud or cluster computing environments
Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning
Use AI coding tools as a central part of how you build software, and can show how you verify the correctness and performance of code you did not write by hand
Have led a technical project with multiple contributors, setting direction and reviewing others' work while continuing to write code yourself
Can explain technical work clearly to both biologists and engineers, in writing (documentation, tutorials) and in person (talks, workshops)

Preferred Qualifications

Depth in both genomics and structural biology
A record as the creator or a core maintainer of a widely used open-source tool in computational biology
Experience managing or formally leading a team of engineers or scientists
A graduate degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience
Proficiency in a systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and experience with performance work on large biological datasets
Experience building software in other areas of computational biology, such as phylogenetics, proteomics, cheminformatics, or high-throughput screen analysis
Experience shipping software built largely with AI coding agents, building agentic systems on large language models, or training machine learning models on biological sequence or structure data

AI has the power to dramatically accelerate the pace of scientific discovery and the development of healthcare interventions. Alongside the models and tools we build for scientists, Anthropic’s life science research teams now run their own wet lab experiments. We’re hiring a life sciences patent counsel to work side-by-side with our researchers as they work to advance biomedical progress.

You will manage patent strategy and filings for our life sciences research, from the first conversation with a scientist through global prosecution. You will also be our in-house expert on the patent questions, many of them new, that arise when scientists use AI as a research tool. You will partner closely with our patents lead (direct manager), the Head of IP, Research Legal, our Life Sciences Counsel, and outside counsel to design and implement a patent program that supports our researchers and partners and is aligned with the company’s mission.

Manage patent strategy and filings for Anthropic’s life sciences research in the U.S. and internationally, including invention harvesting, filing decisions, drafting oversight, prosecution, and management of outside counsel
Serve as the trusted patent advisor to our life science research teams, and design and implement scalable guidance and processes to support our fast-growing life science efforts
Make inventorship determinations for AI-assisted research, and advise on inventor declarations and the duty of candor
Develop claim and filing strategies across biological and chemical inventions, platform technologies, and computational methods, accounting for written description, enablement, eligibility, and obviousness
Partner with Research Legal and Communications on the timing of publications, preprints, presentations, and open-source releases
Advise on the patent aspects of agreements with life science and biopharma counterparties, including ownership of inventions and improvements, and support patent diligence and freedom-to-operate analyses for our research
Anticipate emerging legal developments affecting AI technologies in the life science and biopharma space and provide strategic guidance to leadership

Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based

Substantial hands-on experience drafting and prosecuting U.S. life sciences patent applications, and directing foreign prosecution through local counsel
Lead responsibility for a patent portfolio, including managing budget and outside or foreign counsel
Experience making inventorship determinations and resolving ownership questions in multi-party research arrangements (for example, with universities and other partners)
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate legal risk into practical guidance for scientists, researchers, and business partners
A low-ego, high-empathy orientation and a “doer” attitude: willing to roll up your sleeves and pitch in where needed
Intense curiosity about AI and science, and a commitment to responsible AI development

Role Overview

Plasmidsaurus is hiring a Research Associate to join our R&D team in South San Francisco. You’ll run the experiments that make our RNA-seq products faster to improve and more robust, turning open questions about our workflows into changes our production labs adopt.
You’ll start by running experiments designed by our Scientists and soon be proposing and planning your own. This role is ideal for someone who loves the bench, wants to understand why a protocol works, and wants to see their results show up in products customers use every day.

What You'll Do

Run the experiments.
Execute wet-lab experiments on our RNA-seq workflows, from sample prep through library prep and sequencing.
Learn the molecular biology.
Build a deep understanding of our RNA-seq protocols and the molecular reactions behind each step. You should be able to think in molecular interactions.
Read the data.
Analyze results from your experiments and draw clear conclusions about what worked, what didn't and why.
Propose what's next.
Use those results to suggest and plan new experiments that solve real problems in our workflows.
Keep a clean record.
Document every experiment in a lab notebook so it can be reproduced, then communicate and present results clearly to the team.
Get it into production.
Help carry successful results into changes our production labs can adopt.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means our RNA-seq products get better, faster and more reliable because of the experiments you run.

Your first few months
You're contributing right away. You efficiently complete several planned experiments, document them in your lab notebook and share clear updates on the results.
You know our workflow. You quickly get up to speed and can walk a new teammate through our full RNA-seq protocol and explain the molecular biology behind each step.
You're thinking ahead. You analyze your own results and propose new experiments to solve problems in our workflows.
You're already making a difference. At least one of your results comes with a recommendation that production has adopted or is evaluating.

Your first year
We make decisions based on solid data. You own a line of investigation, and you design, run and interpret the experiments behind it.
Customers depend on more robust products. Improvements you've helped prove out have been adopted by our production labs.
The team understands the chemistry. You're a go-to person for how each step of our protocol works, and you help bring new hires up to speed.
We're moving faster. Open questions become tested answers sooner because you run experiments independently and propose your own.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in biology, biochemistry or a related field
1 or 2 years of post-graduate, hands-on wet-lab experience in molecular biology (academic research or industry)
Demonstrated research experience, supervised or independent, such as a senior thesis, internship or independent lab project

Build.

Own.
You take responsibility for your experiments from plan to result. Your work is tidy and organized, your lab notebook is reproducible, and your results are visible to the team.
Move.
You have a bias to action. You plan and follow complex workflows with care, and keep experiments moving so improvements reach production sooner.

You'll help build our approach to operationalizing science. The ideal candidate is self-directed and has built a career in organizations that hold a high bar for scientific and operational rigor.

Turn research ideas into well-scoped experimental plans with clear milestones and criteria for success
Select and manage the external partners best placed to run each project, and coordinate work that spans more than one

jobs.title: Expansion Microscopy Chemist
jobs.description:
About us:

Eon is building the infrastructure for large-scale connectomics data collection, reconstruction, and brain simulation. Our mission is to enable the safe and scalable development of brain emulation technology, beginning with digital twins of model organisms, ie uploading.

We are developing an end-to-end platform that spans tissue preparation, high-throughput microscopy, large-scale image processing, neural reconstruction, connectome-based modeling, and embodied simulation. We are looking for exceptional engineers and scientists who can help turn biological brain data into usable computational systems.

Role

We are seeking an Expansion Microscopy Chemist to own the chemistry at the front of our connectomics pipeline: turning fixed brain tissue into large, intact, isotropically expanded hydrogel specimens that our microscopes can image and our models can trace. You will develop and run multi-gel expansion protocols (Magnify-, LICONN-, and pan-ExM-style chemistries) at scales well beyond typical expansion microscopy, from mouse slices to whole hemispheric sections of primate and human brain expanded more than 10x, and solve the materials problems that come with that scale: swelling stress and fracture, bubbles and polymerization uniformity, homogenization, signal retention and amplification, and cutting gels with minimal tissue loss.

This is a chemistry and materials role, not a biology role. We are looking for someone who has developed or substantially modified expansion hydrogel chemistry themselves, ideally with training in chemistry, polymer chemistry, or materials science. Experience handling tissue (histology, sectioning, staining) is a strong plus. The role is on-site in San Francisco, where you will help set up and run our expansion lab, working closely with our microscopy, segmentation, and Geneva sample-prep teams.

Responsibilities

Own Eon’s expansion protocols end to end: fixation and anchoring, monomer infusion and gelation, homogenization/disruption, iterative re-embedding and expansion, staining, and signal amplification.
Scale expansion to centimeter-scale tissue (whole mouse, primate, and human brain sections) while keeping samples intact, flat, and isotropic at ≥10x linear expansion.
Diagnose and fix failure modes such as cracking, buckling, trapped bubbles, non-uniform swelling, gel–glass adhesion, and over- or under-digestion, using controlled and well-documented experiments.
Develop methods for cutting and sectioning embedded or expanded gels with minimal tissue loss and fast turnaround.
Improve labeling brightness and contrast together with the microscopy team.
Build reagent QC, SOPs, and sample tracking so protocols are reproducible across our SF and Geneva sites and can be run by technicians.
Set up and run the wet-lab expansion bench in our SF lab space, including safe handling of acrylamide and other hazardous reagents.

Skills And Qualifications

PhD (or equivalent experience) in chemistry, polymer chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or a related field.
Hands-on experience developing or substantially modifying expansion microscopy hydrogel chemistry (e.g., proExM, iterative ExM, X10/TREx, Magnify, pan-ExM, LICONN, tetra-gel), not only applying a published protocol.
Strong grounding in hydrogel and polymer physics: free-radical polymerization, crosslink density, ionic strength and swelling, and mechanical robustness of gels.
A rigorous, systematic experimentalist who designs controlled experiments, keeps excellent records, and quantifies outcomes (expansion factor, isotropy and distortion, defect rates, signal retention).
Able to work independently and on-site in San Francisco.

Nice to have:

Histology and tissue handling (fixation, cryo- or vibratome sectioning, staining of brain tissue); experience with large or thick samples, tissue clearing, or gel sectioning; experience with human or non-human primate tissue; familiarity with fluorescence imaging of expanded samples and how sample prep affects downstream segmentation; prior work at a startup or ExM-focused company.

Representative projects

Taking a human brain hemi-section through our multi-gel protocol to full expansion with no macroscopic cracks, using salt-gradient expansion and mechanical support.
Running a design-of-experiments study on gel composition, initiators, and disruption conditions to make large-sample expansion reliable rather than artisanal.
Developing a low-loss cutting workflow for embedded or expanded tissue and quantifying tissue loss.
Raising signal brightness through amplification chemistry so scans run faster on our microscopes.

Salary and Benefits

$130,000–$190,000 base salary depending on experience, plus equity and benefits.
Opportunity to work in a cutting-edge field that impacts neuroscience and AI safety.

new_jobs.description:
About Sanguine Biosciences, Inc.

Sanguine Biosciences is accelerating personalized medicine research by empowering patients with their healthcare data and making it as easy as possible for them to participate in the medical research process. We partner with patients and pharmaceutical companies to accelerate precision medicine R&D by securely and efficiently collecting and providing patient samples and relevant health data. We are helping thousands of researchers at 20 of the top 40 global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies increase the speed and quality at which they are conducting their research. It is an exciting time; our biotech company is growing quickly and needs the best team members to join us.

The Laboratory Technician I is an entry-level role responsible for the processing of human whole blood and other human biospecimens used for research. Sample processing includes plasma, serum, PBMC, T, B, and NK cell isolations, cell counting, aliquot preparation, sample thawing, and sample storage procedures.

Technicians work primarily in the processing team and rotate into the fulfillment team (kitting, shipping, and sample retrieval) on a scheduled basis. The role works under direct guidance from team leads and senior technicians, builds toward independent sign-off on laboratory procedures, and may progress to Laboratory Technician II.

Primary Responsibilities

Sample Processing & Accessioning
Accurately document and accession biospecimen collection information following company SOPs.
Process whole blood into plasma, serum, and PBMC, including density gradient separation and cryopreservation of PBMCs, following SOPs and with direct guidance until each procedure is signed off.
Process other human biological samples as trained, including urine, stool, saliva, leukopaks, synovial fluid, and skin punch biopsies.
Assist with isolation of immune cell subsets such as T, B, and NK cells from whole blood.
Conduct cell counting, aliquot preparation, and sample thawing.
Assist with routine sample QC, including post-thaw viability, under guidance.
Perform basic laboratory procedures such as cell-based assay work, and assist with flow cytometry and research-grade testing.
Document all work completely, accurately, and at the time it is performed, including sample processing, specimen storage, distribution and transfers, and LIMS entries, in accordance with company standards.
Fulfillment, Rotation & Cross-Training
Prepare and pack biological samples for shipment under guidance, following SOPs and IATA regulations.
Support kit builds and frozen shipment prep on a scheduled rotation with the fulfillment team.
Coordinate and schedule kit shipments with approved couriers in line with established shipping procedures and customer requirements.
Receive, unpack, verify, process incoming deliveries, and help with supply counts and stock levels under the direction of the Biorepository Logistics Lead.
Complete cross-training on a backup team and maintain a current competency record.
Equipment, Safety & Compliance
Support basic troubleshooting of processing and sample storage equipment and escalate issues to team leads.
Participate in the rotating on-call for freezer and system alarms after training.
Participate in a rotating schedule to cover occasional weekend needs, such as special cases and sample deliveries, as required.
Perform routine laboratory equipment maintenance, cleaning, waste disposal, and general laboratory housekeeping in accordance with established SOPs, manufacturer guidelines, and company quality and safety standards. Ensure equipment and workspaces are clean, organized, and maintained in proper working condition, with all activities appropriately documented.
Perform routine laboratory support functions alongside the Biorepository Associates, such as labeling and organizing tubes and racks, preparing workstations and consumables, putting samples away with LIMS location updates, completing freezer and refrigerator temperature checks and equipment logs.
Flag unclear steps, errors, or gaps in the SOPs used to the team lead so they can be corrected.
Follow the company quality management system (QMS), approved SOPs, work instructions, and Good Documentation Practices (GDP), and comply with applicable regulatory and biosafety requirements, to ensure accurate and reproducible work.
Follow safety and EHS procedures, and perform other job functions or special projects as assigned.

Position Requirements

Associate’s degree with at least 1 year of experience in a life science laboratory environment, or [2]+ years as a Biorepository Associate (I or II)
Ability to communicate effectively in verbal and written form.
Intermediate computer skills.
Complete cross-training and be signed off on kit build within 6 months of hire, and on frozen shipment prep under guidance within 12 months.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a life science field
Experience with mammalian blood samples.
Experience working in a biobank or biorepository.

Working Conditions

Must be willing to adhere to infectious disease and immunization protocols.
Must be able to work in a BSL-2 laboratory environment with biohazards and various chemicals and wear appropriate PPE.
Must be able to wear appropriate PPE.
Availability to work full-time shifts Monday through Friday between 7 AM and 7 PM, with occasional weekend availability as needed.
Ability to lift 40 lbs.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Team

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries. The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of demonstrating how AI tools can accelerate scientific workflows and enable discovery.

About The Role

We are hiring Research Associates: early-career bench scientists who will join a small team to help establish our biology research program. This is an entry-level role, great for individuals who have done some research during an undergrad or masters program and may be considering pursuing a PhD in Life Sciences in the future.

You'll work directly alongside senior scientists, executing and troubleshooting experiments at the bench while learning advanced techniques in a fast-moving, highly collaborative environment. We value curiosity, careful hands, and the willingness to take ownership of a result. Our scientists are eager to teach; we're hiring for motivation and trajectory as much as for existing skill.

This is a fully hands-on bench role — while familiarity with computational biology and bioinformatics is welcome, the role does not involve AI/ML model development.

Key responsibilities

Execute molecular biology and biochemistry experiments at the bench under the direction of senior scientists
Maintain meticulous, reproducible records and contribute to shared protocols
Troubleshoot experiments, propose adjustments, and present results clearly in group meetings
Maintain mammalian and bacterial cell lines, materials stocks, and reagent inventories
Learn and adopt new techniques rapidly as projects evolve, with training provided

Minimum Qualifications

Have hands-on research experience in molecular biology, biochemistry, or a closely related field
Are proficient with foundational molecular biology techniques: PCR, gel electrophoresis, molecular cloning, and plasmid preparation
Have experience with aseptic technique and bacterial or mammalian cell culture, and with nucleic acid extraction, purification, and quantification
Follow, document, and adapt experimental protocols with care and precision
Are highly motivated, eager to learn, and energized by hands-on bench work
Are practical and resourceful — you'd rather find a way through than a reason it can't be done
Listen carefully, take feedback well, ask good questions, and are comfortable when priorities shift quickly
Are excited to use AI models as a tool at the bench to plan experiments, interpret data, and decide what to try next

Preferred Qualifications

A BS or MS in molecular biology, biochemistry, chemical biology, microbiology, bioengineering, or a related discipline
Protein expression and purification experience (e.g., affinity, SEC, IEX)
Mammalian cell culture experience, including transfection and stable line maintenance
Enzyme kinetics or quantitative biochemical assay development (fluorescence, absorbance, FRET)
Next-generation sequencing library preparation experience
Familiarity with common bioinformatics workflows and molecular biology software (e.g., sequence analysis, alignment, primer and construct design)
Experience using AI tools such as Claude in a research setting — for literature review, protocol drafting, data interpretation, or experimental troubleshooting

This is a rare opportunity to help define how a frontier AI company does biology. You'll learn quickly, work closely with people who want to teach, and see your results feed directly into how the most capable AI models are evaluated and improved.

Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

About Beneficial Deployments

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About The Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team, focused on helping scientists everywhere get the most from Claude, especially Claude Science. You'll run enablements, workshops and hackathons, build demos that show what frontier models can do for the field, and grow a community of scientists building with Claude. You'll also scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic, so our Applied AI and customer teams can support scientists without you in the room.

Responsibilities

Be the DRI for scientific enablement: decide what to run, build the materials, deliver them, and measure whether research teams reach daily use of Claude.
Lead our programs for activating scientists at scale, such as LSVP and Claude for Researchers: set the goals, design the program and run it.
Build demos, notebooks and tutorials that show scientists what frontier models can do in their own work, and be an active voice where scientists share tools online (X, LinkedIn, etc.).
Scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic: train our Applied AI and Customer Success teams, and build playbooks they can run without you.
Build and lead a scientist community around Claude, and be its ambassador (and support ambassador programs), from small meetups to large conferences.
Be the voice of scientists inside Anthropic: turn what you hear into concrete asks and see them through to launch, and partner with Marketing and Comms so campaigns and content reach the scientific community.

Deep hands-on expertise with AI tools for science such as Claude Science: you know where they shine and where they break.
Real credibility as a scientist: hands-on experience doing science in academic labs, biotechs, pharma or research institutes, ideally as a user of the kind of tools you'll help scientists adopt. Experience building or running programs for scientific communities is a plus.
A track record of helping many scientific teams adopt a new tool through demos, trainings, workshops or hackathons.
Up to date on AI for science, such as agentic analysis and AI co-scientists, and able to explain it to working scientists.

new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain biology software in genomics and structural biology (libraries, command-line tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks) for use by researchers and AI agents, inside Anthropic and externally
Own the path from research code to public release, including testing, validation against reference data and established tools, benchmarking, documentation, and packaging, and make the call on when something is ready to ship
Maintain what we release: triage issues, review outside contributions, and manage breaking changes
Represent the team in the biology community through conferences, workshops, tutorials, and direct work with researchers and maintainers, and turn what you learn about their needs into priorities for the team
Partner with the team's computational and experimental scientists to turn research code into well-tested, reusable software
Lead the technical direction of the projects you own through design review, code review, and mentoring, and, depending on your interests and the team's needs, lead a small team
Build with Claude and AI coding agents as your default way of working, hold agent-written code to the same standard as your own, and set the team's practices for reviewing and validating it

Minimum Qualifications

Have built, released, and maintained biology software that researchers outside your own group use, with evidence of adoption you can point to (for example public repositories, package downloads, citations, or use in other groups' pipelines)
Have deep working expertise in genomics or structural biology, including the data types, file formats, standard tools, and common failure modes of at least one of these fields
Are proficient in Python and comfortable working with large datasets in Linux and cloud or cluster computing environments
Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning
Use AI coding tools as a central part of how you build software, and can show how you verify the correctness and performance of code you did not write by hand
Have led a technical project with multiple contributors, setting direction and reviewing others' work while continuing to write code yourself
Can explain technical work clearly to both biologists and engineers, in writing (documentation, tutorials) and in person (talks, workshops)

Preferred Qualifications

Depth in both genomics and structural biology
A record as the creator or a core maintainer of a widely used open-source tool in computational biology
Experience managing or formally leading a team of engineers or scientists
A graduate degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience
Proficiency in a systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and experience with performance work on large biological datasets
Experience building software in other areas of computational biology, such as phylogenetics, proteomics, cheminformatics, or high-throughput screen analysis
Experience shipping software built largely with AI coding agents, building agentic systems on large language models, or training machine learning models on biological sequence or structure data

new_jobs.title: Research Scientist, Life Sciences (Computational)
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Team

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries. The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-accelerated scientific discovery.

About The Role

We're seeking an exceptional Research Scientist to join the team. This role combines deep computational biology expertise with frontier AI capabilities, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-driven scientific discovery.

As one of the first computational members of this Life Sciences research group, you'll work on a high-impact team that operates at the intersection of computational and experimental biology. You'll bring broad computational biology experience to bear across the team's projects, driving discoveries from large-scale computational analysis of biological data through to results our experimental scientists can test, and moving flexibly between problems as the science demands. You'll have substantial access to Claude and you'll help establish how computational biology operates at Anthropic.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how AI transforms biological research. You'll work with some of the world's best AI researchers while tackling problems that matter deeply for scientific understanding and biomedicine. If you're excited about using your computational expertise to make fundamental biological discoveries and guide the development of transformative AI systems, we want to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

Build, run, and maintain the analysis pipelines that back the team's experimental programs: sequence analysis at petabyte scale, structural bioinformatics, phylogenetic and comparative genomics, design and analysis of high-throughput functional screens, biological sequence modeling, etc.
Partner directly with experimental biologists to design experiments that produce high-quality data, and turn results around fast enough to immediately inform the next experiment
Draw on the literature and curated biological knowledge bases alongside primary data to generate and prioritize hypotheses for experimental follow-up
Stand up and maintain the team's computational infrastructure: data ingestion, workflow orchestration, internal databases, and the interfaces that make all of it accessible to both researchers and AI agents
Use Claude and our internal agent frameworks heavily in your own work, and feed what you learn back to the model-improvement and product teams as evaluations, datasets, and concrete failure cases
Pick up analyses across projects as priorities shift; we're looking for breadth and flexibility over a single deep specialty

Minimum Qualifications

Have a PhD in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, biophysics, machine learning, computer science, or a related quantitative or biological field, or equivalent industry research experience
Have a track record of computational biology research you have led end to end, from question to result, with evidence of impact (for example publications, preprints, released datasets or tools, or research that changed a program's direction)
Have demonstrated breadth across multiple areas of computational biology
Are proficient in one or more programming languages used in scientific computing and comfortable working on large datasets in Linux and cloud compute environments
Can take an ambiguous biological question, scope the analysis, and produce a result an experimentalist can act on
Communicate computational results clearly to both biologists and ML researchers

Preferred Qualifications

Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and developing solutions in rapidly evolving research environments
Are results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
Hands-on experience in experimental biology, or a track record of designing experiments side by side with experimentalists
Experience building tools, pipelines, or agentic systems on top of LLMs, or training models on biological sequence data
Deep expertise in one or two areas of computational biology (for example structural biology, metagenomics, single-cell genomics, or protein design) on top of the required breadth

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$300,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California:
We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. new_jobs.title: Research Scientist, Life Sciences (Chemistry)
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking research scientists with deep expertise in experimental chemistry to join the team. We welcome chemists from across the field, including medicinal, synthetic organic, physical organic, organometallic, inorganic, analytical, physical, and materials chemistry, as well as formulation science. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be an expert in your area of chemistry with hands-on experience designing, and running experiments, from synthesizing, purifying, and characterizing compounds to studying reaction mechanisms and kinetics. Above all, you'll close the loop between AI-generated hypotheses and experimental data to share with the community. Working alongside AI researchers and engineers, you'll drive experimental programs end to end and pressure-test AI-designed molecules, AI-proposed synthetic routes, and AI-predicted mechanisms and properties against real chemistry.

This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Key responsibilities

Depending On Your Area Of Chemistry, You Will

Design multi-step synthetic routes for small molecules and oversee their execution end to end, including route selection, reaction optimization, purification strategy, and interpretation of full characterization data (NMR, LC-MS, HPLC)
Design and run mechanistic, kinetic, and spectroscopic studies to explain and predict reactivity, selectivity, and molecular properties
Prepare and characterize inorganic and organometallic compounds, materials, and formulations, and relate their composition and structure to their properties
Coordinate synthesis and biological evaluation with external contract research organizations and academic partners
Evaluate AI-designed molecules, AI-proposed synthetic routes, and AI-predicted mechanisms and properties, drive them to experimental readout, and feed results back to research teams
Generate experimental and computational data, for example from quantum mechanical calculations, that research teams use to train and evaluate AI models
Apply medicinal chemistry principles, including SAR analysis and physicochemical property optimization, to compound design and prioritization
Ensure experimental data across programs is high quality and well documented, including procedures, spectra, and failure modes
Communicate findings clearly to chemistry, AI research, and life sciences audiences

Minimum Qualifications

PhD in chemistry
Demonstrated depth in your area of experimental chemistry (for medicinal chemists, SAR-driven design and optimization of small molecules,), with recent, sustained hands-on laboratory work
Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of experience in your area of chemistry beyond the PhD
For medicinal chemists, a track record of advancing programs from hit identification through lead optimization
Experience directing chemistry activities at contract research organizations
Computational chemistry, cheminformatics, or coding skills, for example quantum mechanical calculations (DFT) or Python with RDKit or pandas for data analysis and automation
Experience using AI or ML tools in chemistry or the life sciences
Publications and/or patents demonstrating scientific impact

We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Role Overview

Plasmidsaurus is hiring a Research Associate to join our R&D team in South San Francisco. You’ll run the experiments that make our RNA-seq products faster to improve and more robust, turning open questions about our workflows into changes our production labs adopt.
You’ll start by running experiments designed by our Scientists and soon be proposing and planning your own. This role is ideal for someone who loves the bench, wants to understand why a protocol works, and wants to see their results show up in products customers use every day.

What You'll Do

Run the experiments.
Execute wet-lab experiments on our RNA-seq workflows, from sample prep through library prep and sequencing.
Learn the molecular biology.
Build a deep understanding of our RNA-seq protocols and the molecular reactions behind each step. You should be able to think in molecular interactions.
Read the data.
Analyze results from your experiments and draw clear conclusions about what worked, what didn't and why.
Propose what's next.
Use those results to suggest and plan new experiments that solve real problems in our workflows.
Keep a clean record.
Document every experiment in a lab notebook so it can be reproduced, then communicate and present results clearly to the team.
Get it into production.
Help carry successful results into changes our production labs can adopt.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means our RNA-seq products get better, faster and more reliable because of the experiments you run.

Your first few months
You're contributing right away. You efficiently complete several planned experiments, document them in your lab notebook and share clear updates on the results.
You know our workflow. You quickly get up to speed and can walk a new teammate through our full RNA-seq protocol and explain the molecular biology behind each step.
You're thinking ahead. You analyze your own results and propose new experiments to solve problems in our workflows.
You're already making a difference. At least one of your results comes with a recommendation that production has adopted or is evaluating.

Your first year
We make decisions based on solid data. You own a line of investigation, and you design, run and interpret the experiments behind it.
Customers depend on more robust products. Improvements you've helped prove out have been adopted by our production labs.
The team understands the chemistry. You're a go-to person for how each step of our protocol works, and you help bring new hires up to speed.
We're moving faster. Open questions become tested answers sooner because you run experiments independently and propose your own.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in biology, biochemistry or a related field
1 or 2 years of post-graduate, hands-on wet-lab experience in molecular biology (academic research or industry)
Demonstrated research experience, supervised or independent, such as a senior thesis, internship or independent lab project

Nice to have
Experience working with nucleic acids
Experience analyzing experimental data
Experience with NGS library prep or sequencing
Experience with lab automation or liquid-handling robots

Ways of Working

Build.
You're scientifically curious and think in molecular interactions. You want to understand why a protocol works, not just run it.
Own.
You take responsibility for your experiments from plan to result. Your work is tidy and organized, your lab notebook is reproducible, and your results are visible to the team.
Move.
You have a bias to action. You plan and follow complex workflows with care, and keep experiments moving so improvements reach production sooner.
Participate.
You communicate clearly and work closely with the team. You share results early and speak up with ideas for new experiments.
Inspire.
You raise the bar for the people around you, and you help bring new teammates up to speed on our workflows.

We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly align with the job description as we seek out diverse and creative perspectives. Team members who love to learn and collaborate in an inclusive environment will thrive with us. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. The Position

Why Genentech

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Genentech.

We are seeking a machine learning scientist to join our Computational Sciences Center of Excellence as a Postdoctoral Fellow. In this role, you will apply advanced ML techniques to disease biology to significantly impact our understanding of disease biology and the discovery of novel therapeutic interventions. A successful candidate will conduct cutting-edge research at the intersection of machine learning, biology, and drug development. This position offers a unique opportunity to be jointly mentored by experienced machine learning and computational scientists, with close collaboration across Genentech’s research organization.

The Opportunity:

The primary focus of this role is developing deep learning models for multimodal cellular data to decode cell differentiation and predict how interventions alter cellular phenotypes. Specifically, you will build deep representations of T cell biology to better understand T cell differentiation and various phenotypic states from a therapeutic perspective. Leveraging a strong background in machine learning and hands-on experience with deep learning architectures, your research responsibilities will include designing, training, and evaluating generative and conditional models, including transformer-based architectures. In this role, you will collaborate closely with computational and experimental scientists to generate and test biological hypotheses directly relevant to drug discovery.

This is a fantastic opportunity to contribute to world-class science in a leading biotechnology company.

Who You Are:

PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Computational Science, or a related field, with a strong focus on machine learning methods development.
Impactful researcher with first-author publications in leading scientific journals or main tracks in top-tier machine learning conferences.
Strong hands-on experience designing, training, and evaluating deep learning architectures, with particular interest in experience developing generative models or models for conditional prediction.
Strong programming skills in Python, PyTorch, and higher-level libraries (such as huggingface), with experience implementing custom model components and training workflows.
Pragmatic and focused researcher, driven to solve complex scientific problems independently and in a collaborative environment.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate across machine learning and biological disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with generative transformers
Developing models for single-cell or multimodal biological data.
Strong understanding of multi-omics and NGS data
Experience in immunology and T cell biology is a plus.
