new_jobs.title: Expansion Microscopy Chemist
new_jobs.description:
About us:

Eon is building the infrastructure for large-scale connectomics data collection, reconstruction, and brain simulation. Our mission is to enable the safe and scalable development of brain emulation technology, beginning with digital twins of model organisms, ie uploading.

We are developing an end-to-end platform that spans tissue preparation, high-throughput microscopy, large-scale image processing, neural reconstruction, connectome-based modeling, and embodied simulation. We are looking for exceptional engineers and scientists who can help turn biological brain data into usable computational systems.

Role

We are seeking an Expansion Microscopy Chemist to own the chemistry at the front of our connectomics pipeline: turning fixed brain tissue into large, intact, isotropically expanded hydrogel specimens that our microscopes can image and our models can trace. You will develop and run multi-gel expansion protocols (Magnify-, LICONN-, and pan-ExM-style chemistries) at scales well beyond typical expansion microscopy, from mouse slices to whole hemispheric sections of primate and human brain expanded more than 10x, and solve the materials problems that come with that scale: swelling stress and fracture, bubbles and polymerization uniformity, homogenization, signal retention and amplification, and cutting gels with minimal tissue loss.

This is a chemistry and materials role, not a biology role. We are looking for someone who has developed or substantially modified expansion hydrogel chemistry themselves, ideally with training in chemistry, polymer chemistry, or materials science. Experience handling tissue (histology, sectioning, staining) is a strong plus. The role is on-site in San Francisco, where you will help set up and run our expansion lab, working closely with our microscopy, segmentation, and Geneva sample-prep teams.

Responsibilities

Own Eon’s expansion protocols end to end: fixation and anchoring, monomer infusion and gelation, homogenization/disruption, iterative re-embedding and expansion, staining, and signal amplification.
Scale expansion to centimeter-scale tissue (whole mouse, primate, and human brain sections) while keeping samples intact, flat, and isotropic at ≥10x linear expansion.
Diagnose and fix failure modes such as cracking, buckling, trapped bubbles, non-uniform swelling, gel–glass adhesion, and over- or under-digestion, using controlled and well-documented experiments.
Develop methods for cutting and sectioning embedded or expanded gels with minimal tissue loss and fast turnaround.
Improve labeling brightness and contrast together with the microscopy team.
Build reagent QC, SOPs, and sample tracking so protocols are reproducible across our SF and Geneva sites and can be run by technicians.
Set up and run the wet-lab expansion bench in our SF lab space, including safe handling of acrylamide and other hazardous reagents.

Skills And Qualifications

PhD (or equivalent experience) in chemistry, polymer chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or a related field.
Hands-on experience developing or substantially modifying expansion microscopy hydrogel chemistry (e.g., proExM, iterative ExM, X10/TREx, Magnify, pan-ExM, LICONN, tetra-gel), not only applying a published protocol.
Strong grounding in hydrogel and polymer physics: free-radical polymerization, crosslink density, ionic strength and swelling, and mechanical robustness of gels.
A rigorous, systematic experimentalist who designs controlled experiments, keeps excellent records, and quantifies outcomes (expansion factor, isotropy and distortion, defect rates, signal retention).
Able to work independently and on-site in San Francisco.

Nice to have:

Histology and tissue handling (fixation, cryo- or vibratome sectioning, staining of brain tissue); experience with large or thick samples, tissue clearing, or gel sectioning; experience with human or non-human primate tissue; familiarity with fluorescence imaging of expanded samples and how sample prep affects downstream segmentation; prior work at a startup or ExM-focused company.

Representative projects

Taking a human brain hemi-section through our multi-gel protocol to full expansion with no macroscopic cracks, using salt-gradient expansion and mechanical support.
Running a design-of-experiments study on gel composition, initiators, and disruption conditions to make large-sample expansion reliable rather than artisanal.
Developing a low-loss cutting workflow for embedded or expanded tissue and quantifying tissue loss.
Raising signal brightness through amplification chemistry so scans run faster on our microscopes.

Salary and Benefits

$130,000–$190,000 base salary depending on experience, plus equity and benefits.
Opportunity to work in a cutting-edge field that impacts neuroscience and AI safety.
